marrow__ANAT_CH54_Q015.displayText:
The sustentaculum tali is a medial shelf of the calcaneus that supports the talar head and carries the flexor hallucis longus tendon groove below.

The sustentaculum tali is a projection on the medial surface of the calcaneus.

Its superior surface has a facet for the middle facet on the head of the talus and supports the posterior part of the talar head. Its inferior surface has a groove for the tendon of flexor hallucis longus as it enters the sole.

Three ligaments attach to the sustentaculum tali: plantar calcaneonavicular ligament on its anterior surface, deltoid ligament on its medial surface, and the medial talocalcaneal ligament.
emphasis: The sustentaculum tali is a medial shelf of the calcaneus that supports the talar head and carries the flexor hallucis longus tendon groove below

rationales.a: The talus sits on the sustentaculum but the projection itself belongs to the calcaneus.
rationales.c: The navicular lies anterior to the talar head and receives it; it does not bear the sustentaculum projection.
rationales.d: The cuneiforms are distal tarsal bones and do not form the medial calcaneal shelf.
